core.title: Declare each train's themes explicitly, primary theme first
core.given: A train groups themed wagons and may not yet declare a themes list.
core.when: You create a train, touch one lacking an explicit themes list, change its themes or their order, add/remove/move its wagons, or re-theme a member wagon.
core.then: The train declares its themes explicitly as a list whose first entry is its primary theme.
prefer: Most wagons should match the primary (first declared) theme; keep it so when adding, moving or re-theming wagons.
For a train spanning multiple themes, list the dominant theme first, others after as secondary.
On a move, recheck both the train left and the train joined.
avoid: Themes only implied by the train's name or wagons.
Letting most wagons drift to a secondary or undeclared theme.
Listing many secondary themes just to make off-theme wagons look aligned.
unless: Secondary themes are allowed when a train spans multiple themes; not every wagon needs to match the primary.
core.why: The primary theme is the first declared theme, so it exists only if themes are declared explicitly; most wagons matching it keeps the train coherent.
evidence: Each affected train has an explicit, non-empty themes list; its first entry is the primary theme.
For each affected train, the count/ratio of member wagons matching the primary theme is reported (source: most should match).
verification: A check reads each affected train: a missing or empty explicit themes list is flagged as a violation, not treated as unknown or exempt.
The check reads the first declared theme as the primary theme; the general standard for alignment is 'most', not 'all', wagons matching.

The check reports, per affected train, the count or ratio of member wagons matching the primary theme; it reads 'most' as more than half for reporting, invents no stricter threshold, and does not present majority alignment as this rule's mandatory gate (the source strength is 'should'; explicit declaration is the mandatory part).

Recheck scope: every train whose membership changed - including the train a moved or removed wagon left - and every train containing a wagon whose theme changed, not only trains whose own artifact changed.

Train and wagon definition files are identified by path or kind in the planning area; this rule mandates no specific location (its reference realization states none), and wagon files are read because a wagon's theme and membership feed its train's theme fit.
Theme-name canonicality is not checked by this rule; it is covered by the sibling canonicality convention.

values: train touched while lacking an explicit themes list
wagon added to or moved into a train
wagon removed from or moved out of a train (affects source and destination trains)
train themes list added, removed, changed or reordered
theme of an existing member wagon changed (in the wagon artifact or elsewhere)
train has a missing or empty explicit themes list
most of a train's member wagons are off the primary (first declared) theme

fires: Planner creates a new train and assigns wagons to it
Planner touches a train that has no explicit themes list (missing declaration must be fixed, not skipped)
Planner adds or moves wagons into an existing train whose primary theme differs from the new wagons' theme
Planner removes a wagon from a train, or moves a wagon out of one train into another (both trains are rechecked)
Planner reorders a train's themes list, changing which theme is primary
Planner changes the theme of an existing wagon that belongs to a train, even when the train artifact itself is not edited
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon's acceptances without changing its theme or train membership
Editing code or tests outside planning artifacts
Validating that a theme name is canonical (covered by planner.theme.must-be-canonical)

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that are the train and wagon definition files this rule reads; the activation fact file_kind takes its values from these kinds (wagon files matter because a wagon's theme and membership feed its train's theme fit).

neutralityNotes: Trains, wagons and themes are shared planning-model concepts, not stack terms, so given/when/then/why, prefer, avoid, unless and evidence carry over essentially verbatim; the core names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path. The only realization-specific content is the concrete source examples (verifier_detail[1], verifier_detail[2]) and this rule's term/finding/detector ids, all marked bunOnly; core:verification names the checks generically. The cross-reference to planner.theme.must-be-canonical in doesNotFire is a catalog-level rule id, kept as-is (this rule's legacyId equals its PLT-87 id, so catalog ids are shared across realizations). bun.json states no concrete location for train and wagon definition files, so no path profile requirement is made: only roles.plan_artifact.kinds is required, and the source's generic path/kind identification note is retained in core:verification. No vocabulary key was missing, so proposedKeys is empty.
